About the Jukebox

Earth Information Jukebox turns NASA Earth Information Center imagery into music, live in your browser. It reads the pixels of each frame and plays notes from them, so people who can't see the image can still hear how it changes. Nothing is pre-recorded.

How pixels become sound

Mapping from image features to sound
Image featureSoundNote
Cool / blue pixelsDeep warm synth pads150–300 Hz range
Warm / red-yellow pixelsHigher melodic notes500–800 Hz range
BrightnessVolume and low-pass filter openingBrighter = richer harmonics
Sudden frame-to-frame jumpSoft bell chimeLightning, city-light surges

All notes come from the C major pentatonic scale, so any mix of colours stays harmonious.

The three tracks

  • Change in Night Lights (2012–2023): Rhythmic ambient pulses and shimmering bells.
  • Sea Surface Currents & Temperature: Evolving oceanic chords with stereo panning.
  • ISS Lightning Events (2017–2023): A deep atmospheric drone with crisp chimes.

Choosing a year

The year selector jumps the video to the matching point in its date range. Years outside a track's range snap to its first or last frame.

Built by Greenbyte Explorers for NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026. Imagery: NASA Earth Information Center.
